name: Native resolution + integer scaling
oneLiner: A game that stretches its small canvas with CSS (blurry, uneven pixels) becomes pixel-perfect: the canvas keeps drawing at its native size, is shown at the largest whole number of device pixels per game pixel that fits (any devicePixelRatio), centred in a themed border on the same pixel grid, with toGame() mapping taps back to game pixels, an optional fit step for small phones, an optional CRT overlay and a fullscreen toggle. No game logic or timing changes.
fits: any canvas game drawn at a fixed low resolution (256x224, 320x180, 240x160, 256x240...)
platformers, top-down adventures, tactics, turn-based battles, shooters, puzzle
single-file browser games that use width: 100% / max-width: calc(...) to fill the window
notFor: games that resize the canvas backing store to the window (canvas.width = innerWidth): not native-resolution
smooth vector or HD games that should scale fractionally
games drawn into several stacked canvases (wrap each, or scale their common parent instead)

needs: the canvas element the game draws on and its native size (width/height attributes)
every pointer/touch -> game coordinate mapping in the game (kept when it uses the canvas rect ratio, else replaced by toGame)
provides: toGame(clientX, clientY | event) -> native game pixels, inside flag
scale(): device px per game px, css scale, letterbox, canvas rect
fullscreen toggle on the game area

params.label: Max scale (css px per game px, 0 = none)

assets: module/pixel-scaler.js: the element as one dependency-free script (global GameDNA_PixelScaler): layout, device-pixel snapping, border, CRT overlay, fullscreen button, toGame
checks/scaler-check.py, checks/input-check.py: browser measurements (scale, blur, letterbox, mapping; real taps on the two unseen hosts)
